findings.title: Failed result processing is acknowledged and committed
findings.body: The worker catches every exception from `result_processor` and then unconditionally marks the offset complete in `finally`. The commit loop will subsequently commit that offset, so a transient database/API failure permanently drops the result instead of retrying or sending it to a DLQ. This contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing; the added error-handling test also does not wait for the one-second commit loop, so it can pass before the erroneous commit occurs.

findings.title: Negative --max-workers silently drops all consumed messages
findings.body: `--max-workers` accepts arbitrary integers, but a negative value is passed as `num_queues`. `range(num_queues)` then creates no queues or workers; each submission raises while indexing `self.queues`, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches that error and marks the message complete. The commit loop will therefore advance Kafka offsets without processing any results. Reject non-positive worker counts rather than using `max_workers or 20`.

findings.title: The queue pool has no backpressure and can grow without bound
findings.body: Each work queue is constructed as an unbounded `queue.Queue()`, and `submit` always returns after an O(1) enqueue. If a queue's worker is slow or blocked, the consumer continues polling and accumulating full Kafka payloads in memory indefinitely. This defeats the documented natural backpressure and can OOM a consumer during a downstream outage or a hot group; the queues need a bounded capacity and a corresponding pause/blocking policy.

findings.title: Shutdown relies on Python 3.13-only queue APIs
findings.body: `Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On Python 3.12 and earlier, `q.shutdown()` raises `AttributeError`, which is swallowed here, leaving idle workers blocked forever in `get()`. Because workers are joined sequentially with five-second timeouts, shutting down the default 20 queues can take roughly 100 seconds and leaks daemon threads. Use sentinels or timed `get()` calls unless the project has dropped all pre-3.13 runtimes.

findings.title: Closing a strategy disables the worker pool reused by later assignments
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` and reuses it for every `create_with_partitions` call, but this strategy's `close`/`terminate` shuts that shared pool down. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets every worker's shutdown flag and never recreates workers. If the processing strategy is recreated after a partition reassignment/rebalance, the factory hands the new strategy the same dead queues, so newly submitted work is never processed and its offsets remain outstanding. Allocate a fresh pool per strategy assignment or reset/restart the pool before reuse.
